tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. ## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

content.content:
## How It Works

**Network isolation** — iptables firewall blocks all outbound traffic except Anthropic API domains (baked into the image). To allow additional domains, mount a custom allowlist:

```bash
-v /path/to/allowed-domains.txt:/etc/allowed-domains.txt:ro
```

**Workspace** — `/workspace` is writable so Claude can create and edit files. Mount context files read-only at `/workspace/context` for reference (put your `CLAUDE.md` there).

## Limitations

**IP-based firewall** — Domain allowlisting resolves IPs at container start. If Anthropic's CDN/load-balancer IPs rotate during the container's lifetime, connections will fail. Restart the container to re-resolve. This is an inherent limitation of iptables-based filtering.

## Building Locally

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

To pin a specific Claude Code version:

```bash
docker compose build --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.241
```

# Nxeon fork of claudebox (https://github.com/ArmanJR/claudebox, MIT)
FROM node:22-bookworm

# "latest" by default; override with --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.287
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=latest

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Dev tooling so Claude can "set up applications", plus firewall/init tooling.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      git python3 python3-pip python3-venv build-essential ripgrep jq curl \
      ca-certificates procps iptables iproute2 dnsutils sudo tini less \
      unzip zip openssh-client util-linux && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Reuse uid/gid 1000: rename the node image's `node` user/group to `claude`.
RUN groupmod -n claude node && \
    usermod -l claude -d /home/claude -m -s /bin/bash node && \
    mkdir -p /home/claude/.claude /home/claude/.npm-global && \
    chown -R claude:claude /home/claude && \
    echo "claude ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/claude && \
    chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/claude

# Claude Code CLI
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION} && \
    claude --version && \
    npm cache clean --force

ENV HOME=/home/claude \
    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/claude/.claude \
    DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 \
    NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/home/claude/.npm-global \
    PATH=/home/claude/.npm-global/bin:/home/claude/.local/bin:$PATH \
    PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=1 \
    PROJECTS_DIR=/workspace/projects \
    UPLOADS_DIR=/workspace/uploads \
    FIREWALL_MODE=open

COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
COPY allowed-domains.txt /etc/allowed-domains.txt
COPY package.json server.js /opt/claudebox/
COPY lib /opt/claudebox/lib
RUN chmod 755 /entrypoint.sh && \
    mkdir -p /workspace/projects /workspace/uploads /workspace/.tmp && \
    chown -R claude:claude /workspace

WORKDIR /workspace

EXPOSE 3000 4100-4199

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:${PORT:-3000}/health >/dev/null || exit 1

# tini is PID 1 (reaps orphaned dev servers). The entrypoint runs as root to
# install the firewall, then drops to the `claude` user (uid 1000) with
# NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW removed from the bounding set, so even `sudo` inside the
# container cannot alter the firewall.
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "-g", "--", "/bin/bash", "/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["node", "/opt/claudebox/server.js"]

#!/bin/bash
# claudebox entrypoint (Nxeon fork).
# Runs as root under tini: installs the egress firewall, prepares volumes, then
# drops to the `claude` user (uid 1000) and execs the CMD.
set -u

log() { echo "[entrypoint] $*" >&2; }

RUN_USER="${CLAUDEBOX_USER:-claude}"
RUN_UID="$(id -u "$RUN_USER")"
RUN_GID="$(id -g "$RUN_USER")"
FIREWALL_MODE="${FIREWALL_MODE:-open}"

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    SUDO="sudo"
else
    SUDO=""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auth (optional — never fatal). Resolution order inside the CLI:
#   per-run authToken (POST /v2/run body)  >  CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env
#   > mounted credentials file  >  $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREDENTIALS_MOUNT="/run/claude-credentials"
if [ -z "${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -z "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
    if [ -f "$CREDENTIALS_MOUNT" ]; then
        log "Reading OAuth token from mounted credentials file..."
        TOKEN=$(node -e "
            try {
              const c = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('$CREDENTIALS_MOUNT', 'utf8'));
              const t = c.claudeAiOauth && c.claudeAiOauth.accessToken;
              if (t) process.stdout.write(t);
            } catch (e) {}
        ")
        if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
            export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="$TOKEN"
        else
            log "WARNING: could not extract accessToken from $CREDENTIALS_MOUNT"
        fi
    else
        log "No Claude credentials in env (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)."
        log "Server will start with authMode=none; runs may pass 'authToken' in the request body."
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volumes / home
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-/home/$RUN_USER/.claude}"
    for d in "$CLAUDE_DIR" "${PROJECTS_DIR:-/workspace/projects}" /workspace/.tmp "/home/$RUN_USER"; do
        mkdir -p "$d"
        if [ "$(stat -c %u "$d")" != "$RUN_UID" ]; then
            log "chown $d -> $RUN_UID:$RUN_GID"
            chown "$RUN_UID:$RUN_GID" "$d" || true
        fi
    done
    # Fix ownership inside the claude config volume (cheap: only wrong-owned entries).
    find "$CLAUDE_DIR" -xdev \! -user "$RUN_UID" -exec chown "$RUN_UID:$RUN_GID" {} + 2>/dev/null || true
    mkdir -p "${UPLOADS_DIR:-/workspace/uploads}" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [ "${CLAUDE_SUDO:-1}" = "0" ]; then
        rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/claude
        log "sudo disabled for $RUN_USER (CLAUDE_SUDO=0)"
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Firewall
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IPT="$SUDO iptables"
IP6T="$SUDO ip6tables"

fw_fail() {
    log "ERROR: failed to apply firewall rule: $*"
    log "The container needs --cap-add NET_ADMIN. Set FIREWALL_MODE=off to skip (NOT recommended)."
    exit 1
}

ipt()  { $IPT "$@"  || fw_fail "iptables $*"; }
ip6t() { $IP6T "$@" 2>/dev/null || log "ip6tables $* failed (IPv6 unavailable?) — ignoring"; }

nameservers() { awk '/^nameserver/ {print $2}' /etc/resolv.conf; }
GATEWAY_IP=$(ip route 2>/dev/null | awk '/^default/ {print $3; exit}')

allow_dns() {
    for ns in $(nameservers); do
        case "$ns" in
            *:*) ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
                 ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT ;;
            *)   log "Allowing DNS to nameserver: $ns"
                 ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
                 ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ -n "$GATEWAY_IP" ]; then
        log "Allowing DNS to Docker gateway: $GATEWAY_IP"
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$GATEWAY_IP" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$GATEWAY_IP" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
    fi
}

firewall_open() {
    log "FIREWALL_MODE=open: public internet allowed; private/link-local/metadata ranges blocked."
    ipt -F OUTPUT
    ipt -P OUTPUT ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    # Replies to inbound connections (app -> :3000 / :4100-4199) and replies to our own egress.
    ipt -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    allow_dns
    # Optional explicit exceptions (comma separated CIDRs or host:port not supported; CIDRs only).
    if [ -n "${FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS:-}" ]; then
        IFS=',' read -ra extra <<< "$FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS"
        for c in "${extra[@]}"; do
            c=$(echo "$c" | xargs); [ -z "$c" ] && continue
            log "Allowing extra CIDR: $c"
            ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$c" -j ACCEPT
        done
    fi
    # New connections to non-public ranges are dropped. This includes the
    # docker network's own subnet (172.16/12 or 192.168/16): claudebox never
    # initiates connections to the app; replies are covered by ESTABLISHED above.
    for cidr in 0.0.0.0/8 10.0.0.0/8 100.64.0.0/10 127.0.0.0/8 169.254.0.0/16 \
                172.16.0.0/12 192.0.0.0/24 192.168.0.0/16 198.18.0.0/15 \
                224.0.0.0/4 240.0.0.0/4; do
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$cidr" -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-admin-prohibited
    done
    ipt -A OUTPUT -j ACCEPT

    # IPv6: allow global unicast only.
    ip6t -F OUTPUT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -p ipv6-icmp -j ACCEPT          # NDP etc.
    for cidr in fe80::/10 fc00::/7 ::ffff:0:0/96 ::/128 ::1/128 ff00::/8; do
        ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$cidr" -j REJECT
    done
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -d 2000::/3 -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -j REJECT
}

firewall_allowlist() {
    # Original claudebox behaviour: only domains in /etc/allowed-domains.txt.
    local ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE="/etc/allowed-domains.txt"
    log "FIREWALL_MODE=allowlist: only domains in $ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE are reachable."
    ipt -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    allow_dns
    ipt -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT   # temporary, for resolving the allowlist
    if [ -f "$ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r domain || [ -n "$domain" ]; do
            domain=$(echo "$domain" | xargs)
            [[ -z "$domain" || "$domain" == \#* ]] && continue
            log "Resolving $domain..."
            for ip in $(dig +short "$domain" @8.8.8.8 | grep -E '^[0-9.]+$'); do
                log "  Allowing $domain -> $ip"
                ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ip" -j ACCEPT
            done
        done < "$ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE"
    else
        log "WARNING: $ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE not found. No domains will be allowed."
    fi
    ipt -D OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -j DROP
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -j DROP
}

case "$FIREWALL_MODE" in
    open)      firewall_open ;;
    allowlist) firewall_allowlist ;;
    off|none)  log "WARNING: FIREWALL_MODE=$FIREWALL_MODE — no egress filtering applied." ;;
    *)         log "ERROR: unknown FIREWALL_MODE=$FIREWALL_MODE (open|allowlist|off)"; exit 1 ;;
esac
log "Firewall ready (mode=$FIREWALL_MODE)."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Drop privileges and exec
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
export HOME="/home/$RUN_USER"
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    exec setpriv --reuid="$RUN_UID" --regid="$RUN_GID" --init-groups \
        --bounding-set=-net_admin,-net_raw,-sys_admin \
        --inh-caps=-all -- "$@"
fi
exec "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# claudebox entrypoint (Nxeon fork).
# Runs as root under tini: installs the egress firewall, prepares volumes, then
# drops to the `claude` user (uid 1000) and execs the CMD.
set -u

log() { echo "[entrypoint] $*" >&2; }

RUN_USER="${CLAUDEBOX_USER:-claude}"
RUN_UID="$(id -u "$RUN_USER")"
RUN_GID="$(id -g "$RUN_USER")"
FIREWALL_MODE="${FIREWALL_MODE:-open}"

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    SUDO="sudo"
else
    SUDO=""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auth (optional — never fatal). Resolution order inside the CLI:
#   per-run authToken (POST /v2/run body)  >  CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env
#   > mounted credentials file  >  $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREDENTIALS_MOUNT="/run/claude-credentials"
if [ -z "${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -z "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
    if [ -f "$CREDENTIALS_MOUNT" ]; then
        log "Reading OAuth token from mounted credentials file..."
        TOKEN=$(node -e "
            try {
              const c = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('$CREDENTIALS_MOUNT', 'utf8'));
              const t = c.claudeAiOauth && c.claudeAiOauth.accessToken;
              if (t) process.stdout.write(t);
            } catch (e) {}
        ")
        if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
            export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="$TOKEN"
        else
            log "WARNING: could not extract accessToken from $CREDENTIALS_MOUNT"
        fi
    else
        log "No Claude credentials in env (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)."
        log "Server will start with authMode=none; runs may pass 'authToken' in the request body."
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volumes / home
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-/home/$RUN_USER/.claude}"
    for d in "$CLAUDE_DIR" "${PROJECTS_DIR:-/workspace/projects}" /workspace/.tmp "/home/$RUN_USER"; do
        mkdir -p "$d"
        if [ "$(stat -c %u "$d")" != "$RUN_UID" ]; then
            log "chown $d -> $RUN_UID:$RUN_GID"
            chown "$RUN_UID:$RUN_GID" "$d" || true
        fi
    done
    # Fix ownership inside the claude config volume (cheap: only wrong-owned entries).
    find "$CLAUDE_DIR" -xdev \! -user "$RUN_UID" -exec chown "$RUN_UID:$RUN_GID" {} + 2>/dev/null || true
    mkdir -p "${UPLOADS_DIR:-/workspace/uploads}" 2>/dev/null || true
    if [ "${CLAUDE_SUDO:-1}" = "0" ]; then
        rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/claude
        log "sudo disabled for $RUN_USER (CLAUDE_SUDO=0)"
    fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Firewall
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IPT="$SUDO iptables"
IP6T="$SUDO ip6tables"

fw_fail() {
    log "ERROR: failed to apply firewall rule: $*"
    log "The container needs --cap-add NET_ADMIN. Set FIREWALL_MODE=off to skip (NOT recommended)."
    exit 1
}

ipt()  { $IPT "$@"  || fw_fail "iptables $*"; }
ip6t() { $IP6T "$@" 2>/dev/null || log "ip6tables $* failed (IPv6 unavailable?) — ignoring"; }

nameservers() { awk '/^nameserver/ {print $2}' /etc/resolv.conf; }
GATEWAY_IP=$(ip route 2>/dev/null | awk '/^default/ {print $3; exit}')

allow_dns() {
    for ns in $(nameservers); do
        case "$ns" in
            *:*) ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
                 ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT ;;
            *)   log "Allowing DNS to nameserver: $ns"
                 ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
                 ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ns" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ -n "$GATEWAY_IP" ]; then
        log "Allowing DNS to Docker gateway: $GATEWAY_IP"
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$GATEWAY_IP" -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$GATEWAY_IP" -p tcp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
    fi
}

firewall_open() {
    log "FIREWALL_MODE=open: public internet allowed; private/link-local/metadata ranges blocked."
    ipt -F OUTPUT
    ipt -P OUTPUT ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    # Replies to inbound connections (app -> :3000 / :4100-4199) and replies to our own egress.
    ipt -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    allow_dns
    # Optional explicit exceptions (comma separated CIDRs or host:port not supported; CIDRs only).
    if [ -n "${FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS:-}" ]; then
        IFS=',' read -ra extra <<< "$FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS"
        for c in "${extra[@]}"; do
            c=$(echo "$c" | xargs); [ -z "$c" ] && continue
            log "Allowing extra CIDR: $c"
            ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$c" -j ACCEPT
        done
    fi
    # New connections to non-public ranges are dropped. This includes the
    # docker network's own subnet (172.16/12 or 192.168/16): claudebox never
    # initiates connections to the app; replies are covered by ESTABLISHED above.
    for cidr in 0.0.0.0/8 10.0.0.0/8 100.64.0.0/10 127.0.0.0/8 169.254.0.0/16 \
                172.16.0.0/12 192.0.0.0/24 192.168.0.0/16 198.18.0.0/15 \
                224.0.0.0/4 240.0.0.0/4; do
        ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$cidr" -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-admin-prohibited
    done
    ipt -A OUTPUT -j ACCEPT

    # IPv6: allow global unicast only.
    ip6t -F OUTPUT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -p ipv6-icmp -j ACCEPT          # NDP etc.
    for cidr in fe80::/10 fc00::/7 ::ffff:0:0/96 ::/128 ::1/128 ff00::/8; do
        ip6t -A OUTPUT -d "$cidr" -j REJECT
    done
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -d 2000::/3 -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -j REJECT
}

firewall_allowlist() {
    # Original claudebox behaviour: only domains in /etc/allowed-domains.txt.
    local ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE="/etc/allowed-domains.txt"
    log "FIREWALL_MODE=allowlist: only domains in $ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE are reachable."
    ipt -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
    allow_dns
    ipt -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT   # temporary, for resolving the allowlist
    if [ -f "$ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r domain || [ -n "$domain" ]; do
            domain=$(echo "$domain" | xargs)
            [[ -z "$domain" || "$domain" == \#* ]] && continue
            log "Resolving $domain..."
            for ip in $(dig +short "$domain" @8.8.8.8 | grep -E '^[0-9.]+$'); do
                log "  Allowing $domain -> $ip"
                ipt -A OUTPUT -d "$ip" -j ACCEPT
            done
        done < "$ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE"
    else
        log "WARNING: $ALLOWED_DOMAINS_FILE not found. No domains will be allowed."
    fi
    ipt -D OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT
    ipt -A OUTPUT -j DROP
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
    ip6t -A OUTPUT -j DROP
}

case "$FIREWALL_MODE" in
    open)      firewall_open ;;
    allowlist) firewall_allowlist ;;
    off|none)  log "WARNING: FIREWALL_MODE=$FIREWALL_MODE — no egress filtering applied." ;;
    *)         log "ERROR: unknown FIREWALL_MODE=$FIREWALL_MODE (open|allowlist|off)"; exit 1 ;;
esac
log "Firewall ready (mode=$FIREWALL_MODE)."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Drop privileges and exec
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
export HOME="/home/$RUN_USER"
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    exec setpriv --reuid="$RUN_UID" --regid="$RUN_GID" --init-groups \
        --bounding-set=-net_admin,-net_raw,-sys_admin \
        --inh-caps=-all -- "$@"
fi
exec "$@"

input.content:
# claudebox v2 protocol (Nxeon fork)

This document describes the `/v2/*` API that the Nxeon `app` uses to drive Claude Code inside
the `claudebox` container. The original `/prompt`, `/health` and `/v1/*` (OpenAI compat) endpoints
are unchanged.

Verified against **Claude Code 2.1.287** (`claude --help`, real `claude -p` output and the
`sdk-tools.d.ts` shipped in the npm package).

## Authentication

Every `/v2/*` request needs `Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY`.
If `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` is unset, `/v2/*` returns 401 for everything (fail closed) unless
`CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1`. `/health` is unauthenticated.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET  | `/health` | `{status, activeRequests, version, claudeVersion, authMode, activeRuns, queuedRuns, maxConcurrent, firewallMode, autoPermissionMode}`. `authMode` is `oauth` \| `api_key` \| `credentials` \| `none`. |
| POST | `/v2/run` | Start a run; the response **is** the SSE stream (see below). |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId/events?fromSeq=N` | SSE: replay buffered events with `seq >= N` (inclusive, default 1), then follow live. Also honours the standard `Last-Event-ID` header (resumes at `id+1`) when `fromSeq` is absent. Ends immediately after replay if the run is finished. 404 if the run is unknown/expired. |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId` (alias `/v2/runs/:runId`) | Run info JSON (see `GET /v2/runs`). |
| POST | `/v2/abort` | `{runId}` → kills the run's whole process group (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 4 s). Queued runs are just dequeued. → `{ok, runId, found, status}` (`status: "aborting"` for a running run). 404 if unknown. |
| GET  | `/v2/runs` | `{runs:[RunInfo], running, queued, retained, maxConcurrent}` — active (queued + running) runs. `?all=1` includes finished runs still retained. |
| POST | `/v2/preview/start` | `{projectSlug, port, command?}` → PreviewStatus (200) / 400 / 409 (port busy) / 422 (cannot detect a command). |
| POST | `/v2/preview/stop` | `{projectSlug, port?}` → `{stopped, ...PreviewStatus}`. Also kills any *unmanaged* process listening on the port (e.g. a dev server Claude started via Bash), except running Claude runs. |
| GET  | `/v2/preview/status?projectSlug=&port=` | PreviewStatus. `port` optional (defaults to the managed port). |
| GET  | `/v2/previews` | `{previews:[PreviewStatus]}` |

`RunInfo = {runId, projectSlug, status: queued|running|done|error|aborted, mode, model, sessionId, pid, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt, exitCode, lastSeq, firstSeq, subscribers}` (times are epoch ms).

`PreviewStatus = {projectSlug, running, managed, listening, port, pid, kind: "process"|"static"|null, command, startedAt, exitCode, logTail: string[] (≤200 lines)}`.
`running = managed || listening` — `listening` comes from a TCP connect probe to `127.0.0.1:<port>` (and `::1`),
so a server Claude started itself is reported as running (with `managed: false`).

Errors are JSON `{error: "message"}` with an appropriate status.

### POST /v2/run body

```json
{
  "runId": "uuid (optional; generated if absent)  ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$",
  "prompt": "string",
  "projectSlug": "my-app",              // ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$ ; cwd = $PROJECTS_DIR/<slug> (created if missing)
  "sessionId": "claude session id | null",   // → --resume
  "model": "opus|sonnet|haiku|<full id>",    // → --model
  "mode": "auto|edit|plan|ask",              // default auto
  "thinking": "off|normal|max",              // → env MAX_THINKING_TOKENS 0 / 8000 / 32000 (unset = CLI default)
  "effort": "low|medium|high|xhigh|max",     // optional → --effort
  "attachments": ["/workspace/uploads/<id>/<file>"],
  "appendSystemPrompt": "string",            // → --append-system-prompt
  "maxTurns": 50,                            // → --max-turns
  "previewPort": 4123,                       // 4100-4199 → env PORT/HOST/BASE_PATH for Claude's shell
  "authToken": "optional per-run token"
}
```

* Attachments must resolve inside `$UPLOADS_DIR` or the project dir; each is appended to the
  prompt as `[Attached file: <path> — use Read tool]`. `--add-dir $UPLOADS_DIR` is always passed so
  Read works in every mode.
* `authToken` overrides the container env for that run: tokens starting with `sk-ant-api` are set
  as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` removed); anything else (e.g. `sk-ant-oat01-…`

| raw CLI line | normalized |
|---|---|

| `stream_event` `content_block_delta` `thinking_delta` | `thinking {delta}` |

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` | — | Bearer token for `/v2/*` (and `/v1/*` if set). Required. |
| `CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH` | `0` | `1` = allow `/v2/*` without a key (dev only). |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | — | Default Claude auth (optional; per-run `authToken` overrides). |
| `PORT` | `3000` | API port. |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT` | `4` | Max simultaneous runs (and legacy `/prompt` requests). |
| `PROJECTS_DIR` | `/workspace/projects` | Project root (cwd = `<dir>/<slug>`). |
| `UPLOADS_DIR` | `/workspace/uploads` | Allowed attachment root (mount read-only). |
| `PREVIEW_PORT_MIN` / `PREVIEW_PORT_MAX` | `4100` / `4199` | Allowed preview ports. |
| `PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOST` | `claudebox` | Passed to vite via `__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. |
| `RUN_RETENTION_MS` | `1800000` | How long finished runs stay replayable. |
| `AUTO_PERMISSION_MODE` | `bypassPermissions` | Permission mode used for `mode=auto` (`auto` to use the classifier mode). |
| `CLAUDE_BIN` | `claude` | CLI binary (tests point this at `test/mock-claude.js`). |
| `FIREWALL_MODE` | `open` | `open` \| `allowlist` \| `off`. |
| `FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS` | — | Comma-separated private CIDRs to exempt in `open` mode. |
| `CLAUDE_SUDO` | `1` | `0` removes the claude user's sudo rights at startup. |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `/home/claude/.claude` | Claude Code state (sessions for `--resume`, `.claude.json`, credentials). Mount a volume here. |
| `OPENAI_COMPAT` | `0` | Original OpenAI-compatible endpoints. |

## Firewall (entrypoint, needs `--cap-add NET_ADMIN`)

`open` mode (IPv4 `OUTPUT`): accept `lo`; accept `ESTABLISHED,RELATED` (replies to inbound
connections from the app on :3000 / :4100-4199 and to our own egress); accept DNS to the
`/etc/resolv.conf` nameservers and the default gateway; **reject** new connections to
`0/8 10/8 100.64/10 127/8 169.254/16 172.16/12 192.0.0/24 192.168/16 198.18/15 224/4 240/4`
(covers the docker network's own subnet and cloud metadata); accept everything else.

IPv6: accept `lo`, established, ICMPv6; reject `fe80::/10 fc00::/7 ::ffff:0:0/96 ::1 ff00::/8`; accept `2000::/3`; reject rest.

The entrypoint runs as root, then drops to `claude` (uid 1000) via `setpriv` with `NET_ADMIN`,
`NET_RAW`, `SYS_ADMIN` removed from the bounding set — so even `sudo` inside the container cannot
modify the firewall. `allowlist` mode is the original claudebox behaviour (`/etc/allowed-domains.txt`).

# claudebox v2 protocol (Nxeon fork)

This document describes the `/v2/*` API that the Nxeon `app` uses to drive Claude Code inside
the `claudebox` container. The original `/prompt`, `/health` and `/v1/*` (OpenAI compat) endpoints
are unchanged.

Verified against **Claude Code 2.1.287** (`claude --help`, real `claude -p` output and the
`sdk-tools.d.ts` shipped in the npm package).

## Authentication

Every `/v2/*` request needs `Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY`.
If `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` is unset, `/v2/*` returns 401 for everything (fail closed) unless
`CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1`. `/health` is unauthenticated.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET  | `/health` | `{status, activeRequests, version, claudeVersion, authMode, activeRuns, queuedRuns, maxConcurrent, firewallMode, autoPermissionMode}`. `authMode` is `oauth` \| `api_key` \| `credentials` \| `none`. |
| POST | `/v2/run` | Start a run; the response **is** the SSE stream (see below). |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId/events?fromSeq=N` | SSE: replay buffered events with `seq >= N` (inclusive, default 1), then follow live. Also honours the standard `Last-Event-ID` header (resumes at `id+1`) when `fromSeq` is absent. Ends immediately after replay if the run is finished. 404 if the run is unknown/expired. |
| GET  | `/v2/run/:runId` (alias `/v2/runs/:runId`) | Run info JSON (see `GET /v2/runs`). |
| POST | `/v2/abort` | `{runId}` → kills the run's whole process group (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 4 s). Queued runs are just dequeued. → `{ok, runId, found, status}` (`status: "aborting"` for a running run). 404 if unknown. |
| GET  | `/v2/runs` | `{runs:[RunInfo], running, queued, retained, maxConcurrent}` — active (queued + running) runs. `?all=1` includes finished runs still retained. |
| POST | `/v2/preview/start` | `{projectSlug, port, command?}` → PreviewStatus (200) / 400 / 409 (port busy) / 422 (cannot detect a command). |
| POST | `/v2/preview/stop` | `{projectSlug, port?}` → `{stopped, ...PreviewStatus}`. Also kills any *unmanaged* process listening on the port (e.g. a dev server Claude started via Bash), except running Claude runs. |
| GET  | `/v2/preview/status?projectSlug=&port=` | PreviewStatus. `port` optional (defaults to the managed port). |
| GET  | `/v2/previews` | `{previews:[PreviewStatus]}` |

`RunInfo = {runId, projectSlug, status: queued|running|done|error|aborted, mode, model, sessionId, pid, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt, exitCode, lastSeq, firstSeq, subscribers}` (times are epoch ms).

`PreviewStatus = {projectSlug, running, managed, listening, port, pid, kind: "process"|"static"|null, command, startedAt, exitCode, logTail: string[] (≤200 lines)}`.
`running = managed || listening` — `listening` comes from a TCP connect probe to `127.0.0.1:<port>` (and `::1`),

     (zero-dep, in the claudebox process) serving that dir under `/preview/<slug>/` (and also without
     the prefix, for strip-prefix proxies), path-traversal safe, `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
* Stop: SIGTERM to the group, SIGKILL after 3 s; then any other listener on that port is killed too.
* Vite's host check: requests are accepted for `Host: claudebox[:port]`, localhost and IPs.
  The app's preview proxy should therefore send `Host: claudebox:<port>` (http-proxy `changeOrigin: true`)
  — or the project's vite config must set `server.allowedHosts`.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` | — | Bearer token for `/v2/*` (and `/v1/*` if set). Required. |
| `CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH` | `0` | `1` = allow `/v2/*` without a key (dev only). |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | — | Default Claude auth (optional; per-run `authToken` overrides). |
| `PORT` | `3000` | API port. |
| `MAX_CONCURRENT` | `4` | Max simultaneous runs (and legacy `/prompt` requests). |
| `PROJECTS_DIR` | `/workspace/projects` | Project root (cwd = `<dir>/<slug>`). |
| `UPLOADS_DIR` | `/workspace/uploads` | Allowed attachment root (mount read-only). |
| `PREVIEW_PORT_MIN` / `PREVIEW_PORT_MAX` | `4100` / `4199` | Allowed preview ports. |
| `PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOST` | `claudebox` | Passed to vite via `__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. |
| `RUN_RETENTION_MS` | `1800000` | How long finished runs stay replayable. |
| `AUTO_PERMISSION_MODE` | `bypassPermissions` | Permission mode used for `mode=auto` (`auto` to use the classifier mode). |
| `CLAUDE_BIN` | `claude` | CLI binary (tests point this at `test/mock-claude.js`). |
| `FIREWALL_MODE` | `open` | `open` \| `allowlist` \| `off`. |
| `FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS` | — | Comma-separated private CIDRs to exempt in `open` mode. |
| `CLAUDE_SUDO` | `1` | `0` removes the claude user's sudo rights at startup. |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `/home/claude/.claude` | Claude Code state (sessions for `--resume`, `.claude.json`, credentials). Mount a volume here. |
| `OPENAI_COMPAT` | `0` | Original OpenAI-compatible endpoints. |

## Firewall (entrypoint, needs `--cap-add NET_ADMIN`)

`open` mode (IPv4 `OUTPUT`): accept `lo`; accept `ESTABLISHED,RELATED` (replies to inbound
connections from the app on :3000 / :4100-4199 and to our own egress); accept DNS to the
`/etc/resolv.conf` nameservers and the default gateway; **reject** new connections to
`0/8 10/8 100.64/10 127/8 169.254/16 172.16/12 192.0.0/24 192.168/16 198.18/15 224/4 240/4`
(covers the docker network's own subnet and cloud metadata); accept everything else.
REJECT (icmp-admin-prohibited) is used rather than DROP so blocked tools fail fast instead of hanging.
IPv6: accept `lo`, established, ICMPv6; reject `fe80::/10 fc00::/7 ::ffff:0:0/96 ::1 ff00::/8`; accept `2000::/3`; reject rest.

The entrypoint runs as root, then drops to `claude` (uid 1000) via `setpriv` with `NET_ADMIN`,
`NET_RAW`, `SYS_ADMIN` removed from the bounding set — so even `sudo` inside the container cannot
modify the firewall. `allowlist` mode is the original claudebox behaviour (`/etc/allowed-domains.txt`).

input.command:
E="sudo docker exec -u claude cbtest-box"
echo "npm:   $($E curl -sS -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://registry.npmjs.org/)"
echo "pypi:  $($E curl -sS -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://pypi.org/simple/)"
echo "github: $($E git ls-remote https://github.com/ArmanJR/claudebox HEAD 2>&1 | cut -c1-20)"
echo "meta:  $($E curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://169.254.169.254/ 2>&1)"
GW=$(sudo docker network inspect cbtest -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'); echo "gw=$GW"
echo "gw22:  $($E curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null telnet://$GW:22 2>&1)"
echo "host public ssh (control): $(timeout 5 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/139.99.125.21/22' && echo open-from-host)"
echo "10/8:  $($E curl -sS -m 5 http://10.0.0.1/ 2>&1)"
echo "sudo iptables -F attempt: $($E sudo iptables -F OUTPUT 2>&1)"
echo "rules intact: $(sudo docker exec cbtest-box iptables -S OUTPUT | wc -l)"
$E bash -c 'id; ps -o pid,user,comm 1; cat /proc/self/status | grep CapBnd'

input.command:
sudo docker restart cbtest-box >/dev/null; timeout 60 bash -c 'until sudo docker logs --since 20s cbtest-box 2>&1 | grep -q listening; do sleep 1; done'
echo "rules: $(sudo docker exec cbtest-box iptables -S OUTPUT | wc -l)"
GW=172.18.0.1
echo "control (no firewall container) gw22: $(sudo docker run --rm --network cbtest --entrypoint bash nxeon/claudebox:latest -c "timeout 5 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/$GW/22' && echo REACHABLE || echo unreachable" 2>&1)"
echo "control meta: $(sudo docker run --rm --network cbtest --entrypoint curl nxeon/claudebox:latest -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://169.254.169.254/ 2>&1)"
C="sudo docker run --rm --network cbtest --entrypoint curl nxeon/claudebox:latest -sS -H Authorization:Bearer\ k1 -H Content-Type:application/json"
$C -X POST http://cbtest-box:3000/v2/preview/start -d '{"projectSlug":"fwtest","port":4150,"command":"id; grep CapBnd /proc/self/status; sudo iptables -F OUTPUT; echo flush-exit=$?; sudo -n true && echo sudo-ok; ip route; timeout 5 bash -c \"echo > /dev/tcp/172.18.0.1/22\" && echo GW-REACHABLE || echo gw-blocked; curl -sS -m5 -o /dev/null -w \"npm=%{http_code}\\n\" https://registry.npmjs.org/"}' >/dev/null
timeout 30 bash -c 'until $0 http://cbtest-box:3000/v2/preview/status?projectSlug=fwtest | grep -q "process exited"; do sleep 1; done' $C
$C http://cbtest-box:3000/v2/preview/status?projectSlug=fwtest | jq -r '.logTail[]'
echo "rules after: $(sudo docker exec cbtest-box iptables -S OUTPUT | wc -l)"

input.message:
## claudebox fork: done. Image `nxeon/claudebox:latest` is built and verified, and all 20 tests pass.

Everything is under `/opt/nxeon-workspace/claudebox/`. Nothing is committed and no other directories were touched.

### What was built
- **`Dockerfile`**
  - Based on `node:22-bookworm`. Claude Code is installed at `latest` by default and can be pinned with `ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`; it is currently 2.1.287.
  - Adds the tooling from the brief: git, python3/pip/venv, build-essential, ripgrep, jq, curl, procps, iptables, iproute2, dnsutils, sudo, plus a few extras (unzip, ssh client).
  - The image's `node` user is renamed to `claude`, keeping uid/gid 1000.
  - `HOME=/home/claude` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/claude/.claude`, so sessions and `.claude.json` persist in the volume.
  - npm's global prefix is in the claude user's home, so Claude can run `npm i -g` without root.
  - tini is PID 1, started with `-g`. There is also a HEALTHCHECK.
- **`entrypoint.sh`**
  - Runs as root. It sets up the firewall, creates and chowns the `.claude` and projects directories, then drops to uid 1000 using `setpriv`.
  - NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW and SYS_ADMIN are removed from the capability bounding set. I verified that `sudo iptables -F` fails from processes started by the server. sudo still works for everything else (`CLAUDE_SUDO=0` disables it).
  - Missing credentials are never fatal.
- **`server.js`, `lib/normalizer.js`, `lib/runs.js`, `lib/preview.js`, `lib/static.js`**
  - The original `/prompt`, `/health` and `/v1/*` endpoints are kept.
  - At startup the server reads `claude --version` and `--help` to detect which flags the installed CLI supports.
- **Tests:** `test/mock-claude.js` mimics the real stream-json output and `test/v2.test.js` covers the new behaviour. Run them with `npm test`.
- **Docs:** `PROTOCOL.md` (flags, raw-to-normalized mapping table, endpoints, env vars), a "Nxeon fork" section in `README.md`, and a new MIT `LICENSE` crediting ArmanJR.

### Verified in the running container (temporary network, now cleaned up)
- `/health` returns `{version:"1.0.0-nxeon", claudeVersion:"2.1.287", authMode:"none", ...}`. Calling `/v2` without the bearer token returns 401.
- **Real `claude -p`, no credentials:** `init` → `error{code:"authentication_failed", message:"Not logged in · Please run /login"}` → `result{isError:true}` → `done{exitCode:1}`.
- **Real `claude -p`, fake OAuth `authToken`:** reached api.anthropic.com, got "401 OAuth access token is invalid", and produced the same event sequence.
- **Mock run:** the full normalized stream came through with `id` 1–24 and no duplicated text. Replay with `?fromSeq=20` worked.
- **Abort:** gives `done{exitCode:143, aborted:true}` and leaves no zombie processes.
- **Firewall in open mode:**
  - npm, pypi and github are reachable.
  - 169.254.169.254, 10/8 and the docker gateway's port 22 are blocked. Without the firewall the gateway's port 22 is reachable, so the block is real.
  - Inbound connections from the app to :3000 and :4100 work.
- **Static preview:** port 4100 serves `/preview/site/`.

### Endpoints (all `/v2/*` need `Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY`; `/health` doesn't)
- `POST /v2/run` → the response is the SSE stream.
- `GET /v2/run/:runId/events?fromSeq=N` → SSE replay, then follows live. `fromSeq` is inclusive and defaults to 1; the `Last-Event-ID` header is honoured if `fromSeq` is absent.
- `GET /v2/run/:runId` → run info.
- `POST /v2/abort {runId}`
- `GET /v2/runs` (add `?all=1` to include finished runs)
- `POST /v2/preview/start {projectSlug, port, command?}`
- `POST /v2/preview/stop {projectSlug, port?}`
- `GET /v2/preview/status?projectSlug=&port=`
- `GET /v2/previews`

### Env vars
- **Key and auth:** `CLAUDEBOX_API_KEY` (required — if unset, `/v2` rejects everything unless `CLAUDEBOX_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1`), `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optional).
- **Server and runs:** `PORT=3000`, `MAX_CONCURRENT=4`, `RUN_RETENTION_MS=1800000`, `AUTO_PERMISSION_MODE=bypassPermissions`, `CLAUDE_BIN=claude`, `OPENAI_COMPAT`.
- **Directories:** `PROJECTS_DIR=/workspace/projects`, `UPLOADS_DIR=/workspace/uploads`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- **Previews:** `PREVIEW_PORT_MIN/MAX=4100/4199`, `PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOST=claudebox`.
- **Firewall and sudo:** `FIREWALL_MODE=open|allowlist|off`, `FIREWALL_ALLOW_CIDRS`, `CLAUDE_SUDO=1`.

### What the app server must know
1. **SSE format:** each frame is `id: <seq>\nevent: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n`.
   - `seq` starts at 1 per run and appears only in the `id:` line, not inside `data`.
   - The first frame is `retry: 2000`, and there is a `: ping` comment every 15 s.
   - `done` is always the last event, and the server closes the stream right after it.
   - Response headers include `X-Run-Id` and `X-Run-Status`.
2. **Queueing and reattaching:**
   - Queued runs keep the stream open and emit nothing until they start.
   - A duplicate `runId` returns 409 — reattach through the events endpoint instead.
   - A client disconnect never kills a run; only `/v2/abort` does.
3. **Extra fields on events.** These go beyond `protocol.ts` but don't change it:
   - **Subagent fields:** `parentId` on `tool_use`, `tool_result` and `usage` for subagent activity. Subagent text is never emitted as main `text`.
   - **`usage`:** it is incremental, so sum the events for totals.
   - **`todo`:** items may carry `id` and `activeForm`.
   - **`error`:** has a `code` (`authentication_failed`, `process_exit`, `spawn_error`, `error_max_turns`, …).
   - **`result`:** adds `subtype`, `terminalReason` and `permissionDenials`.
   - **`done`:** may add `aborted:true` and `signal`.
   - **`init`:** adds `permissionMode` and `claudeCodeVersion`.
4. **Todos:** Claude Code 2.1.x in `-p` mode uses TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList rather than TodoWrite. Both are mapped to `todo`, which always carries the full list.
5. **Preview status shape:** `{projectSlug, running, managed, listening, port, pid, kind, command, startedAt, exitCode, logTail: string[]}`.
   - `running` means either we manage the process or something answers a TCP probe on the port, so a server Claude started itself counts as running.
   - Stop also kills whatever is listening on that port, except a Claude run that is still in progress.
6. **Preview proxy and Vite:** the proxy should send `Host: claudebox:<port>` (`changeOrigin: true`). Vite blocks unknown hosts, and the preview env whitelists only `claudebox` via `__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
   - Static sites are served by a built-in server under `/preview/<slug>/`, and also without the prefix.
   - Vite is started with `--base /preview/<slug>/`. Next.js apps must set `basePath` from `BASE_PATH` themselves.
